# Incident Report — Koi Stealer Infection, 2024-09-04 (MTA Exercise)

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (confirmed via DHCP option 12 and NBNS) |
| AD domain / workgroup | bepositive.com (NetBIOS: BEPOSITIVE) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **afletcher** (from Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, both to DC 172.17.0.17 and reflected on 172.17.0.99) |
| Domain controller | 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com, MAC 00:23:ae:50:ba:fd) |

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). Attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not just behavioral — the local Suricata/ET ruleset fired `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) directly on the `/foots.php` POST traffic to 79.124.78.197, corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1` (50 hits, same stream). Behavioral traits also fit: hardcoded IP C2 (no DNS resolution), disguised `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` POST beacons using a spoofed old-IE user agent, and a bot-ID checkin protocol.

## 3. Timeline / Infection Chain

- **17:35:04 UTC** — `172.17.0.99` opens a TLS session (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) to **46.254.34.201:443**. Over the next ~102 seconds this single session pulls **~701 KB** down to the host — consistent with the malware payload being fetched from a compromised/malicious site over HTTPS (contents not recoverable — traffic is TLS-encrypted, no session keys in evidence).
- **17:35:07 UTC** (~2.5s after payload download starts) — first C2 beacon: `POST /foots.php HTTP/1.1` to **79.124.78.197:80**, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, User-Agent spoofed as IE7/Win10. Response: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, empty body.
- **17:35:11 UTC** — `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U HTTP/1.1` to 79.124.78.197. Server responds in plaintext: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — a bot-ID / task-checkin token.
- **17:35:12 UTC** — `POST /index.php` to the same server, 105-byte binary/encrypted response body (config or task data, not human-readable).
- **17:35–~18:34 UTC** — sustained beaconing: **96 `POST /foots.php` requests** to 79.124.78.197 over the capture, spanning from t+155.9s to t+3564.6s (~57 minutes), all with identical spoofed IE7 UA and octet-stream bodies — classic C2 heartbeat/exfil channel.
- Coincident lower-severity Suricata noise on `172.17.0.99 -> 172.17.0.17` (SMBv1 session setup, NTLMSSP unicode ASN.1 overflow signature, IPC$ access, SMB_COM_TRANSACTION, Kerberos principal overflow signature) — these are generic/overly-broad SMB and Kerberos IDS signatures firing on normal domain-joined-host <-> DC SMB/Kerberos traffic, not independent evidence of lateral movement; no second internal host shows compromise indicators.

## 4. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the pcap)

**C2 endpoint (confirmed via signature match):**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP) — POST `/foots.php` (beacon, 96 hits) and GET/POST `/index.php` (checkin)

**Suspected payload-delivery host (traffic observed, contents encrypted):**
- `46.254.34.201:443` (TLS) — SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`

**URLs (cleartext, observed in HTTP requests):**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php`
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php`
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U`

**Bot/task ID (from plaintext C2 response body):**
- `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`

**Malicious/suspicious domain:**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (resolves to 46.254.34.201 — TLS SNI only; no DNS query for this name appears in the capture, meaning resolution happened before/outside this capture window or via a cached/hardcoded lookup)

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. No cleartext HTTP object transfer (file download, `Content-Disposition`, or executable signature) is present anywhere in the capture. The only sizeable transfer (~701 KB from 46.254.34.201) is entirely inside a TLS 1.3 session with no decryption keys available, so no filename or SHA256 can be stated. All traffic to the confirmed C2 (79.124.78.197) is small POST/GET beacon traffic, not a bulk file transfer.

## 5. Notes on What Is NOT an Indicator

- `bepositive.com` / `win-ctl9xbq9y19.bepositive.com` — legitimate internal AD domain, not attacker infrastructure.
- Traffic to `msftconnecttest.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `msn.com`, `bing.com`, `office.com`, `microsoftonline.com`, `godaddy.com` (sso), `lencr.org`, `adobe.com` (`acroipm2.adobe.com/assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt`) — standard Windows/Office/Adobe telemetry and update-check background noise, unrelated to the infection.

## 6. Summary

`172.17.0.99` (DESKTOP-RNVO9AT, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher**, was infected with **Koi Stealer** after retrieving a payload over TLS from `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201). The malware immediately established C2 to **79.124.78.197:80**, checking in via `/index.php` and beaconing continuously via `POST /foots.php` for the remainder of the ~1-hour capture (96 beacons total). Attribution to Koi Stealer is signature-confirmed by the ETPRO ruleset. No file artifact or hash could be extracted because the initial payload transfer was TLS-encrypted.
